project.name: TWINFORGE — Visual intelligence lab
project.productType: SAM image-only perception, causal motion forecasts, locked prediction challenges

typography.sans: System sans-serif; Inter is a non-required first preference in Motion lab.
typography.mono: ui-monospace, SF Mono, Menlo, Consolas, monospace
typography.language: English by default; original provider text remains preserved in exported logs.

shadows.policy: Subtle stage and dialog separation; no decorative glow or full-page card grid.

motion.policy: Explicit playback controls; reduced-motion preference respected. No changes to physics integration or evaluation are part of the visual refresh.

design.density: Primary stage first, compact controls, one subordinate model-decision inspector on desktop. Settings, evidence, recording and optional model tools are progressively disclosed.

stageColors.note: Stage/material/result colors are semantic rendering colors, separate from the shared light interface palette.

design.stageTreatment: Dark simulation and camera stages inside light interface chrome.

preferredPrimitives: Native navigation links, buttons, labeled inputs and select controls
Native dialog sheets with scrollable content and native focus/Escape behavior
Existing Three.js scenes and on-device camera overlay with actual measurements
patterns: Vertical Descriptive Stepper inside expanded model log only (29866)

must: At least 44px touch targets and visible keyboard focus.
Only calculated metrics and geometry; freeze paths before replay.
State that initial state and known planar contact law are supplied.
Identify the arbitrary experiment threshold and instantaneous actuator assumption.
Show failed proposals, sensitivity failures and absence of a passing tested action.
No independent accuracy claim for same-model replay.
Keep local scanner frames on device and separate pixels from physical units.
Use English for all public page copy, dynamic controls, captions and display explanations; preserve original model receipts.
Keep Meta proposals, local numerical predictions and on-device image tracking visibly distinct.
Keep the user-provided mpcdetails.mp4 video as a reference only; never publish third-party footage or frames.
avoid: Claiming real robotic control or reconstruction from synthetic inputs.
Presenting deterministic search as a Meta model invocation.
Keeping water/orbit in the main product.

decisions: Replace the former dark dashboard shell with consistent light chrome across Decision lab, Motion lab and Camera. Keep the simulation and camera stages dark for visual contrast.
Use #cf4b08 for primary buttons and #b94006 on hover. The previous #e95d14 button color was darkened after contrast review; existing canvas orange is unchanged.
Remove permanent navigation sidebars and metric-card grids. Keep the experiment central and reveal settings, raw evidence and advanced tools on demand.
The three navigation links are Decision lab, Motion lab and Camera. The selected page is visually and semantically indicated.
Use the inspected 1279 toolbar, 25010 scrollable sheet and 27028 disclosure patterns as native HTML/CSS. Retain 26923 for horizontal navigation and 29866 only for the detailed model log.
Reject 4880 because retrieved component and demo mismatch. Do not install or adapt that candidate.
Decision lab foregrounds the recorded Muse Spark proposals, actual rejection/verification results, and the distinction between model suggestions and a separate local numerical search.
Motion lab exposes one scene selector and Start/Pause/Reset group. Numerical integration is unchanged; camera framing and decorative environments are presentation-only.
Camera starts from one primary action. Optional examples, video import, exports, recording and limitations are collapsed. Tracking remains local and pixel-based.
User-rejected water and orbit presentations remain out of public navigation; historical code and evidence remain archived.
Keep the user-provided MPC video as an unshipped visual reference, not as a product asset.

A fresh real SAM mask starts the scene. User lock pauses synthetic time, reveal advances it, later visual error remains visible. Live camera cannot be paused and is labeled accordingly.

21st Filmstrip Scrub 29384 informs timecodes, temporal ticks and preview framing; Usage Dashboard 31642 informs actual remaining-allowance display. Native HTML/CSS/ES modules, no sample metrics or decorative fake signals.
A mobile Lock prediction shortcut is beside scene controls. Desktop source and overlay share an aspect-preserving surface. Automatic randomization is opt-in to preserve continuous observation.
